reason: The cited evidence confirms that the base alloy forms Cr-V-rich precipitates (E1) and that radiation-induced precipitation contributes to hardening (E2), but it provides no specific support for the key premises that Hf addition will suppress precipitation, avoid introducing defects, or maintain low hardening; these are speculative extensions not grounded in the cited passages.
premises: Hf addition modifies thermodynamic phase stability in W-Ta-Cr-V to suppress Cr-V-rich precipitation
Suppressing Cr-V-rich precipitates will maintain negligible irradiation hardening
Hf addition does not introduce additional irradiation defects (e.g., dislocation loops)
The base alloy W38Ta36Cr15V11 forms Cr-V-rich precipitates under irradiation at ~8 dpa, 1073 K
Hf can be incorporated into the BCC solid solution without destabilizing the nanocrystalline structure
